t: Minimize Array Sum Using Divisible Replacements
o: Repeatedly, an element divisible by another element can be replaced by that divisor; we want the minimum achievable total. Key observation: divisibility is transitive, so an element x can ultimately become the smallest value in the array that divides x (any longer chain x -> v -> w implies w | x directly). Example 2: 4 and 8 both reduce to 2, giving 2+2+2+3 = 9; example 3 has no divisibility pairs so nothing changes. With values up to 1e5, a harmonic-sieve marking the smallest array divisor of every possible value answers each element in O(1).
k: By transitivity of divisibility, the final value of x is min(x, smallest array element dividing x).
A sieve over multiples of each distinct array value computes the smallest divisor-from-array for every value up to max in O(V log V).
The total can reach 1e10, so use 64-bit accumulation.

a.n: Approach 1: Check Distinct Values per Element
a.i: Sort the distinct values; for each element, scan upward and take the first distinct value that divides it — that is automatically the smallest possible replacement. Simple and clearly correct, though quadratic in the worst case.
s: For each x, scan distinct values ascending; the first v with x % v == 0 is the best replacement for x.
Add min(x, v) to the answer.
a.t: O(n * d) where d is the number of distinct values — up to ~1e10 worst case, acceptable only for favorable inputs

a.i: Build best[v] = smallest array element dividing v by iterating each distinct value s and relaxing all multiples of s (harmonic series gives about V ln V operations). Then each element's contribution is min(x, best[x]) in O(1).
s: Let V = max(nums); initialize best[v] = v for all v.
For each distinct s in nums, for each multiple m of s up to V, set best[m] = min(best[m], s).
Answer is the sum of min(x, best[x]) over all elements.
a.t: O(V log V + n) — the double loop is the harmonic sum over distinct values

w: Lead with the transitivity insight — it collapses the multi-step process into a single 'smallest array divisor' lookup. Pitfalls: assuming only one operation matters (chains are covered by transitivity), 32-bit overflow of the sum, and scanning all pairs O(n^2) which is too slow. Follow-ups: minimum number of operations to reach the minimum sum, or the same question when replacements must use distinct target indices.
